title: SLO-adaptive suspend/resume preemptor with KV segmentation
creator: Lena Zhou
description:
Motivation: Continuous batching with tight GPU memory (quantized models + large KV caches) leads to brittle preemption decisions. Full eviction/restart of in-flight slices causes latency spikes and wasted compute. We need a preemption strategy that minimizes user-visible latency SLO violations while preserving fairness across tenants and reducing KV churn on GPUs.

Goal: Implement an SLO-adaptive suspend/resume preemptor that can pause lower-priority slices, preserve compact KV segments in GPU memory, and resume slices when capacity recovers. The preemptor should: 1) score running slices by SLO risk and progress, 2) select candidates for suspend vs. full termination, 3) shrink or migrate KV segments selectively (hot segment retention), and 4) integrate with tenant-weighted fairness policies.

Scope: Prototype on a single-node serving runtime with continuous batching enabled. Support model-agnostic KV segmentation (per-tenant, and per-model hotset hints). Provide telemetry hooks to validate SLO outcomes and KV residency churn. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, unit and integration tests, and an A/B experiment (canary) comparing to the current full-preemptor baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Preemptor implements suspend/resume API for in-flight slices and integrates with existing batch lifecycle manager
SLO scoring model (latency risk + remaining tokens) is computed per-slice and used to decide suspend vs kill
KV cache can mark and protect up to N hot segments per-tenant during suspension to avoid cold-start costs (configurable N)
End-to-end experiments show <=10% additional tail latency vs baseline for high-priority tenants and >=25% reduction in wasted GPU cycles under preemption-heavy load
Automated unit tests and integration tests cover suspend/resume, KV segment protection, and fairness arbitration
Telemetry dashboards and alerts (SLO drop, preempt churn) created and linked
design_decisions: Use suspend/resume rather than checkpoint/restore to avoid large NVMe roundtrips; suspension keeps minimal per-slice ephemeral state on GPU and marks user KV segments as retained
KV segmentation will be logical (segment IDs) mapped to physical GPU residency; per-tenant quotas prevent hotset monopolization
SLO scoring uses a weighted function: 0.6*deadline_headroom_score + 0.3*remaining_token_fraction + 0.1*tenant_priority_score
Fairness policy: proportional-share across tenant weights, but suspendable quota reserved for bursty high-priority traffic to meet SLAs

When memory pressure persists beyond a configurable grace period, suspended slices are either resumed (when capacity frees) or gracefully drained (with partial response fallback) depending on SLO risk
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit/integration tests + dev runtime validation on small cluster (2 GPUs).
Phase 1: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic on staging region; compare preempt churn and tail latency vs baseline for same workload traces.
Phase 2: Expand to 25% with telemetry gating (SLO degradation < 1.5x, wasted cycles reduced).
Phase 3: Full rollout behind feature flag with operator controls (N hot segments per-tenant, suspend timeout, SLO weight coefficients).
telemetry_queries: Metric: preempt.suspend.count by tenant and model (1m rollup)
Metric: preempt.kill.count by tenant and reason
Metric: kv.segment.residency_seconds by segment_id and tenant
SLO: p99 latency by tenant before/after preempt events
Alert: sustained suspend count > 100/min AND p99 latency increase > 1.2x
